newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen says foreign states have hand in kidnappings.
newsitem.headline: Yemen says foreign states have hand in kidnappings.

text.p: Yemen's prime minister on Wednesday said unspecified foreign countries were behind a series of kidnappings of foreigners in the Arab state.
"Foreign states are behind the kidnappings of foreigners which aim to distort Yemen's image and hinder the election process," said Abdul-Aziz Abdul-Ghani.
"We have evidence that external elements are behind the kidnappings, although the perpetrators are Yemenis," he told a news conference ahead of Sunday's parliamentary elections.
Abdul-Ghani refused to name the countries which he said played a role in the abductions.
Yemeni opposition newspapers have repeatedly pointed the finger at Saudi Arabia following kidnappings.
Abdul-Ghani refused to comment when asked by reporters if Saudi Arabia was behind any of the abductions.
In recent years Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners to use as bargaining chips.
The hostages have included German and French tourists, American oilmen and Western dilpomats who are usually kidnapped in remote areas of Yemen while on outings.
The hostages have been released unharmed but some have said they have felt their lives were in danger.
Yemeni security forces earlier this month secured the release of four German hostages after firing artillery shells near their abductors' hide-out and arrested the kidnappers.
Yemen, a small independent oil-producer, is hoping tourism will boost its weak economy and officials are eager to assure the outside world that the country is safe.
